title: p0481
universal_lens: Means-end manifolds form a directed acyclic graph M = (V, E) where vertices V are goal-objects and edges E are means-object transitions weighted by sign-gestalt expectation kernels. The field decomposes into chain (serial) and lever (parallel) submanifolds with topological invariants: hierarchical depth, mutual alternativeness index, and closure deficit.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference over means-end fields: posterior P(goal|means) ∝ P(means|goal)P(goal) where likelihood P(means|goal) is a conformal predictor over sign-object/signified-object pairs. Chain successions yield Markovian transitions; lever successions induce mixture-of-experts posteriors with mutual alternativeness as gating weights.
gse_mapping: State-transition system S = (X, U, f) where X = goal-object hierarchy, U = means-object selections, f: X×U → X encodes means-end relations. Chain successions are deterministic transitions; lever successions are stochastic with tool-affordance distributions. Closure hierarchicalness defines Lyapunov function for convergence to ultimate goal-object.

The sign-gestalt expectation K_SG(s,σ) is the fundamental measurement operator — it couples sign-objects (observables) to signified-objects (latent goals) via conditional probability. This induces a Bayesian structure: P(goal|means) ∝ K_ME(means,goal)P(goal). The manifold \mathcal{M} decomposes into two dynamical regimes via χ(π): chain successions (serial, Markovian, deterministic planning) and lever successions (parallel, mixture-of-experts, tool-mediated). Topological invariants — hierarchical depth τ, mutual alternativeness entropy, closure deficit — serve as Lyapunov functions for convergence. Breakdown occurs when polysemy breaks K_SG bijectivity, when non-ergodic drift violates stationary K_ME, or when hybrid successions violate χ exclusivity. The mathematical unification is a fiber bundle: base space = goal hierarchy, fibers = means-object selections, connection = sign-gestalt expectation.
